name: CORREL
description: CORREL returns the Pearson product-moment correlation coefficient for two data sets, measuring the strength and direction of their linear relationship.
tldr: Pearson correlation coefficient between two arrays.

parameters.name: array1
parameters.description: The first set of independent (or paired) numeric values.

parameters.name: array2
parameters.description: The second set of numeric values, the same length as array1.

basicExample.explanation: The two series move closely together; the coefficient is near 1, indicating a strong positive linear relationship.

advancedExamples.title: Correlation from ranges
advancedExamples.description: Both ranges must have the same number of points
advancedExamples.explanation: Excel pairs B2 with C2, B3 with C3, and so on, so mismatched sizes cause #N/A.

advancedExamples.title: Negative relationship
advancedExamples.description: Higher price tends to lower demand
advancedExamples.explanation: A coefficient close to -1 means the two variables move in opposite directions linearly.

howItWorks: CORREL computes r = Σ((x - x̄)(y - ȳ)) / sqrt(Σ(x - x̄)² · Σ(y - ȳ)²), where x̄ and ȳ are the means. The result always lies between -1 and 1: 1 is a perfect positive linear relationship, -1 a perfect negative one, and 0 no linear relationship. Text, logicals, and empty cells are ignored in each array.

howToSteps.name: Arrange paired data
howToSteps.text: Put the two related series in equal-length ranges.

howToSteps.name: Read the coefficient
howToSteps.text: Values near 1 or -1 indicate strong linear association.

limitations: Measures only linear association; it can be near 0 even when a strong non-linear relationship exists.
Both arrays must contain the same number of data points, or #N/A is returned.
If either array has zero variance (all identical values), the function returns #DIV/0!.

commonErrors.cause: The two arrays have different numbers of data points.
commonErrors.fix: Make sure array1 and array2 are the same length.

commonErrors.cause: One of the arrays has no variance (all values equal).
commonErrors.fix: Use data with variation, or check for constant columns.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: CORREL works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same result as Excel; PEARSON is also available and equivalent.

faq.question: Is CORREL the same as PEARSON?
faq.answer: Yes. In both Excel and Google Sheets, CORREL and PEARSON return the identical Pearson coefficient.

faq.question: What does a correlation of 0 mean?
faq.answer: It means there is no linear relationship; a non-linear relationship may still exist.

faq.question: Does correlation imply causation?
faq.answer: No. Correlation only measures association, not cause and effect.
